message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to building a well‑rounded leg routine—whether you’re a beginner or a seasoned lifter.  
Feel free to mix and match based on your goals (strength, hypertrophy, endurance, mobility) and the equipment you have.

---

## 1️⃣ Core Compound Movements  
These recruit multiple joints and muscle groups, making them the most efficient for overall leg development.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Typical Sets/Reps | Equipment |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Back Squat** | Quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, core | 3–5 × 4–8 (strength) or 3–4 × 8–12 (hypertrophy) | Barbell + squat rack |
| **Front Squat** | Quads, core, upper back | 3–4 × 6–10 | Barbell + squat rack |
| **Deadlift (Conventional)** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps | 3–5 × 4–8 | Barbell |
| **Romanian Deadlift** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back | 3–4 × 8–12 | Barbell or dumbbells |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | 3–4 × 8–12 per leg | Dumbbells or barbell |
| **Step‑Up** | Quads, glutes, calves | 3–4 × 10–15 per leg | Bench or box + dumbbells |

> **Tip:** Keep your torso upright, knees tracking over toes, and avoid letting hips drop too far forward.

---

## 2️⃣ Isolation & Targeted Movements  
Great for finishing a workout or focusing on lagging areas.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Typical Sets/Reps | Equipment |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | 3–4 × 10–15 | Leg press machine |
| **Hamstring Curl (lying or seated)** | Hamstrings | 3–4 × 10–15 | Machine or cable |
| **Calf Raise (standing or seated)** | Gastrocnemius, soleus | 4–5 × 12–20 | Calf raise machine or dumbbells |
| **Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust** | Glutes, hamstrings | 3–4 × 10–15 | Barbell or bodyweight |
| **Cable Lateral Band Walks** | Glute medius | 3–4 × 15–20 per side | Cable or resistance band |

> **Pro tip:** For glutes, focus on squeezing at the top of the hip thrust or bridge; for hamstrings, keep a slight bend in the knee during curls.

---

## 3️⃣ Bodyweight & Functional Variations  
Perfect for home workouts, mobility work, or as a warm‑up.

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | Typical Sets/Reps | Equipment |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Bodyweight Squat** | Quads, glutes | 3–4 × 15–25 | None |
| **Jump Squat / Plyo Squat** | Quads, glutes, calves | 3–4 × 8–12 | None |
| **Walking Lunge** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | 3–4 × 20 steps | None |
| **Single‑Leg Romanian Deadlift** | Hamstrings, glutes, balance | 3–4 × 8–12 per leg | Dumbbells or kettlebell |
| **Wall Sit** | Quads, glutes | 3–4 × 30–60 sec | None |
| **Resistance Band Lateral Walk** | Glute medius | 3–4 × 15–20 per side | Resistance band |

> **Safety note:** Keep your core engaged and avoid letting your knee collapse inward during lunges or step‑ups.

---

## 4️⃣ Sample Weekly Routine (3‑Day Split)

| Day | Focus | Example Workout |
|-----|-------|-----------------|
| **Day 1 – Strength** | Heavy compound lifts | Back squat 5×5, Romanian deadlift 4×6, Bulgarian split squat 3×8, calf raise 4×12 |
| **Day 2 – Hypertrophy** | Volume + isolation | Front squat 4×8, leg press 4×12, hamstring curl 4×12, glute bridge 3×15 |
| **Day 3 – Mobility & Endurance** | Light load + functional | Bodyweight squat 3×25, walking lunge 3×20, jump squat 3×10, wall sit 3×45 sec |

> Adjust sets/reps based on your training phase (e.g., 4×4 for strength, 4×12 for hypertrophy).

---

## 5️⃣ Warm‑Up & Cool‑Down

| Warm‑Up | Duration | Purpose |
|---------|----------|---------|
| 5–10 min light cardio (bike, row, jog) | 5–10 min | Increase blood flow |
| Dynamic stretches (leg swings, hip circles) | 5–7 min | Mobilize joints |
| Light warm‑up sets (50% of working weight) | 2–3 sets | Prepare muscles |

| Cool‑Down | Duration | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Static stretching (hamstrings, quads, calves, glutes) | 5–10 min | Reduce stiffness |
| Foam rolling | 5–7 min | Release myofascial tension |

---

## 6️⃣ Common Mistakes & How to Avoid Them

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Knees caving inward | Focus on hip external rotation, use a mirror or video feedback |
| Hips dropping too low | Keep chest up, engage core, use a lighter weight if needed |
| Not fully extending the knee | Pause at the bottom, then drive through the heel |
| Over‑reliance on one exercise | Rotate between squats, lunges, and deadlifts to hit all angles |

---

### Bottom Line

- **Compound lifts** build the foundation (strength & mass).  
- **Isolation moves** finish the workout and target weak spots.  
- **Bodyweight/functional drills** improve mobility, balance, and serve as great warm‑ups or recovery days.  

Mix these elements, listen to your body, and progressively overload to see consistent gains. Happy lifting!
